_comment: Committed regression baseline, captured ON THE RUNNER by .github/workflows/benchmark-baseline.yml -- not on a developer machine, which is what every baseline before v3.4.0 was. Generated from the MEDIAN of four consecutive 'npm run benchmark -- --json' runs. Regenerate by dispatching that workflow and merging the branch it pushes; running the capture locally produces a developer-machine baseline and now says so in _machine. A baseline moved without a stated reason is a gate switched off quietly. The TOLERANCE here is 50% and was briefly 20%; see toleranceRationale for why the measurement that supported 20% was too narrow and what disproved it.
toleranceRationale: 50%, after 20% was tried and DISPROVEN by CI within the hour. The cross-instance study (docs/internal/measurements/v3.4.0-runner-baseline.md) measured three captures 16 minutes apart and found a worst spread of 6.7% between their medians; on that evidence 20% looked generous. Four real CI runs on this branch then split two-pass / two-fail, with To Hex (100KB) at -41.8%, To Hex (10KB) at -37.0%, Entropy (100KB) at -26.2% and Frequency distribution (100KB) at -29.2% -- while Regular expression got 24-28% FASTER on the same run. Both directions at once, on tasks no commit in the branch touches: the benchmark imports src/node/index.mjs, which does not reach any changed module. The pool is heterogeneous in memory bandwidth, and three captures within one window sampled one class of host. 50% is what the OBSERVED spread supports. The tolerance is not the interesting number any more -- the baseline being runner-captured is, because it removes the systematic -9.6% machine offset that 50% previously had to absorb ON TOP of this variance.
_machine: Captured on a GitHub Actions runner (Linux/X64), workflow run 33868225945. This is the machine class the regression gate executes on, so the comparison is like against like and the cross-machine offset that limited every earlier baseline does not apply.
